relevant_files.role: Template for language implementation (model as per issue)

conventions.commits: Conventional Commits format with GPG signing (-S) and sign-off (--signoff)
conventions.testing: Unit tests in same file with #[cfg(test)] mod tests; integration tests in crates/*/tests/
conventions.linting: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -- -D warnings, cargo deny check advisories licenses
conventions.error_handling: Result types with thiserror; no unwrap() in production code paths

patterns: Query constants: ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY
Handler functions: extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, find_method_for_receiver, extract_inheritance
LanguageInfo struct registration in get_language_info() match arm
get_ts_language() match arm for Language object retrieval
SPDX header on all .rs files: SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 aptu-coder contributors

related_issues.title: Add Swift grammar support via tree-sitter-swift 0.7.3
related_issues.relevance: Primary task - add Swift language support following Java pattern

constraints: Must add tree-sitter-swift 0.7.3 to workspace dependencies in Cargo.toml
Must create swift.rs module following java.rs template
Must register swift in get_language_info() and get_ts_language() match arms
DEFUSE_QUERY constant required for definition-use site extraction (used by SemanticExtractor)
All new files must include SPDX license header
Must pass cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -- -D warnings, cargo test
test_coverage: Language registration has unit tests in mod.rs (test_get_language_info_known, test_get_language_info_unknown, test_get_ts_language_known, test_get_ts_language_unknown). Individual language modules have integration tests for query compilation and extraction functions (e.g., java.rs has test_extract_function_name, test_find_receiver_type, test_java_element_query_happy_path, test_java_extract_inheritance, test_defuse_query_write_site).

library_findings.notes: Rust crate exposes LANGUAGE constant compatible with tree-sitter 0.26.x API. MIT licensed. Grammar supports .swift files.
Core parsing library used by all language handlers. Swift grammar must be compatible with this version.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Full Java-style implementation
approaches.description: Create swift.rs following java.rs template exactly: define all query constants (ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY), implement all handler functions (extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, find_method_for_receiver, extract_inheritance), and register in mod.rs match arms.
pros: Complete feature parity with other languages
Full DEFUSE_QUERY support for def-use analysis

approaches.name: Approach 2: Minimal implementation with stubs
approaches.description: Create swift.rs with minimal query constants (ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY) and stub handlers returning None. Add DEFUSE_QUERY as required. Register in mod.rs. Defer full implementation to follow-up PR.
pros: Can iterate based on real usage

approaches.name: Approach 3: Kotlin-style implementation
approaches.description: Follow kotlin.rs pattern which has comprehensive handlers. Kotlin is similar to Swift (modern, typed, JVM/native target) so query structures may be more similar than Java.
pros: Kotlin patterns may map better to Swift

recommendation: Approach 1 (Full Java-style implementation) is recommended because: (1) The issue explicitly references modeling after java.rs; (2) DEFUSE_QUERY is required for proper def-use analysis which is a core feature; (3) Complete implementation avoids technical debt and follow-up work; (4) The project already has well-tested patterns for all handler functions.
